verdict.rationale: doola documents outbound webhooks. It sends signed HTTP POSTs (X-Doola-Signature, an HMAC-SHA256 keyed with your webhook secret), and formation and EIN milestones fire real webhooks that sandbox endpoints can trigger for testing. However, the evidence never shows how a consumer registers an endpoint or chooses which events to subscribe to, and the only events shown are formation and EIN milestones. missing for 10: documented endpoint registration and subscription management, a full event-type catalog, delivery/retry semantics, independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: doola sends a POST with an X-Doola-Signature header: an HMAC SHA256 hex digest of the raw request body, keyed with your webhook secret.
Two sandbox-only endpoints complete the formation and EIN milestones on demand, firing the real webhooks
